Here is a cohesive, fully integrated 12-week couch-to-5K plan for your client, now incorporating:
- Running progression with intervals, tempo work, and a Parkrun-style test in Week 8
- Dedicated tempo run day
- Structured, progressive strength program (2 days/week)
- Finisher/race-day prep week ( Week 11 integrated, with Week 12 as final taper/5K test)
- Asthma safety, warm-ups, cold-air considerations, and recovery guidance

Overview of weekly structure
- Running: 3 sessions per week (Tues, Thu, Sat)
- Tempo day: integrated into the running plan (dedicated tempo blocks on select days)
- Interval work: 1–2 sessions per week (Tue/Thu) with progressive load
- Strength: 2 days per week (non-consecutive when possible)
- Cross-training (XT): optional on off days for active recovery
- Parkrun-style test: Week 8 (5K time-trial-like benchmarking)
- Finisher/race-day prep: Week 11
- Week 12: Final taper and race-day or final test

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 — Foundation and habit formation
Goals:
- Build routine, low-to-moderate effort, establish run/walk pattern
- Begin gentle interval exposure and introduce a tempo element
- Establish movement quality and core stability via strength

Weeks 1–3 details
- Running plan (3 days/week):
  - Week 1:
    - Session A: Run/Walk Confidence
      - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes brisk walk + dynamic leg work
      - Main: 1 min jog / 2 min walk x 6 (≈18 min total)
      - Cool-down: 5 min easy walk + calves/hip flexor stretches
    - Session B: 30s jog / 90s walk x 8
    - Session C: XT 20–30 minutes easy (bike, swim, or brisk walk)
  - Week 2:
    - Session A: 1:30 total with jogs/walks
      - 1 min jog / 2 min walk x 8
    - Session B: 90s jog / 2 min walk x 6
    - Session C: XT 20–30 minutes easy
  - Week 3:
    - Session A: 2 km target via run/walk (2 min jog / 2 min walk x ~6)
    - Session B: 1.5–2.0 km continuous if doable (or 3x3 min jog with 2 min walk)
    - Session C: XT 25–30 minutes
- Strength (2 days/week, Day A Lower/Core; Day B Upper/Core)
  - Day A: Goblet squats 3x10–12; RDL 3x10; Glute bridges 3x12; Single-leg deadlift 2x8/leg; Walking lunges 2x10/leg; Plank 3x30–45s
  - Day B: Push-ups 3x8–12; Dumbbell/DB rows 3x8–12; Pallof press 3x8–12/side; Band face pulls 3x12; Farmer’s carries 2x30–45s; Side planks 2x20–30s/side
  - Mobility included pre/post

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 — Build volume; introduce tempo and early longer runs
Goals:
- Increase running time and reduce walk recovery
- Introduce tempo cues and longer continuous blocks where possible
- Maintain asthma safety; adjust as needed

Weeks 4–6 running plan (3 days/week)
- Week 4:
  - Session A: Interval progression
    - 3 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk x 5
  - Session B: 6–8 minutes jog continuous + 2 min walk x 1–2
  - Session C: XT 25–35 minutes
- Week 5:
  - Session A: 4 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk x 4
  - Session B: 8–10 minutes jog continuous if tolerable
  - Session C: XT 25–35 minutes
- Week 6:
  - Session A: 6 minutes jog / 1–1.5 minutes walk x 3
  - Session B: 12 minutes jog continuous if able; otherwise 6x2 minutes jog with 2 minutes walk
  - Session C: XT 30 minutes
- Tempo integration (Weeks 4–6):
  - Week 4: add 6–8 minute tempo within a 25–30 minute run
  - Week 5: tempo 8–10 minutes
  - Week 6: tempo 10–12 minutes; occasional 4–6 minute tempo block if breathing controlled

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 — Longer runs; tempo and intervals at higher intensity
Goals:
- Progress toward longer continuous runs
- Include tempo blocks and longer intervals to approach 5K pace

Weeks 7–9 running plan
- Week 7:
  - Session A: 15–18 minutes continuous jog (or 15 with minimal walk); optional 4–6 min tempo within
  - Session B: 2x10 minutes jog with 2 minutes walk; include 4–6 min tempo in one interval
  - Session C: XT 30–40 minutes
- Week 8 (Parkrun-style test incorporated):
  - Session A: Tempo 10–12 minutes within 20–25 min run
  - Session B: Parkrun-style 5K test day
    - Warm-up: 10–12 minutes easy + dynamic
    - 5K test at steady, controlled pace (target: sustainable pace)
    - Cool-down: 10 minutes easy jog + mobility
  - Session C: XT or easy recovery 20–30 minutes
- Week 9:
  - Session A: 25 minutes continuous at brisk but conversational pace; include 6–8 minutes near tempo
  - Session B: 2x12 minutes jog with 2 minutes walk; try 4–6 minute tempo within if controlled
  - Session C: XT 35–45 minutes

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 — Peak tempo and race readiness; finisher week included
Goals:
- Peak tempo and intervals orient toward 5K pace
- Parkrun/test data used to calibrate Week 10–12 pacing
- Finisher/race-day prep week to consolidate routines and pacing

Weeks 10–12 running plan
- Week 10:
  - Session A: 28–32 minutes continuous with 5–8 minute tempo block in middle
  - Session B: 3x10 minutes jog with 2 minutes rest; middle 5 minutes at brisk pace
  - Session C: XT 30–40 minutes
- Week 11 (Finisher / Race-Day Prep Week):
  - Day 1: Easy + strides; 10–12 min easy, 6x20s strides, 5–8 min easy, 4–6 min tempo
  - Day 2: Light mobility/core; optional light goblet squats and hip hinges
  - Day 3: Tempo + short intervals (8–10 min tempo; 4x1 min at goal pace with 90s rest)
  - Day 4: XT or rest
  - Day 5: Long run with race-pace finisher (40–45 minutes easy; finish with 2x5 minutes at race pace)
  - Day 6: Rest or mobility
  - Day 7: Race-day rehearsal or Parkrun-day mimic (optional)
- Week 12 (Final test and taper):
  - Day 1: 20–25 minutes easy with 4–6 x strides
  - Day 2: 15–20 minutes gentle jog + mobility
  - Day 3: 5K test if EIA controlled; otherwise 4–5K at comfortable-to-brisk pace
  - Final: Race-day readiness, hydrate, fuel, and reconstructively taper before the real Parkrun or 5K

Strength component (2 days/week, integrated with running)
- Phase-aligned progression (Weeks 1–3 → Phase 2 → Phase 3 → Phase 4)
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Lower/Core Day A; Upper/Core Day B (as listed previously)
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Increase sets to 4x for main lifts; add tempo cues; 5–10 min mobility post
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength endurance with 4x6–8 rep schemes; add unilateral work; core circuit integrated
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Heavy but controlled strength with 4x5–6 for main lifts; keep volume moderate to avoid fatigue before race days
- Tempo/pace cues in strength (optional): minimal, explosive reps only if breathing remains controlled

Nutrition, recovery, and asthma notes
- Pre-run fuel: light snack 30–60 minutes prior if needed; avoid heavy meals right before
- Hydration: 6–8 cups water daily; increase around running
- Post-run: protein + carbs within 1–2 hours
- Iron/Vitamin D/B12: monitor status; consult GP if fatigue persists
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly
- Inhaler: carry and use as prescribed; warm air considerations on cold days (mask/scarf)

Progression and safety reminders
- Gradual increases of 10–15% weekly volume where feasible
- EIA management: pause if symptoms; adjust intensity; seek medical advice if persistent
- Cross-training remains optional for recovery or to manage fatigue
- If any joint pain or persistent fatigue occur, scale back and reassess

Want a printable calendar?
- I can generate a week-by-week calendar with:
  - Exact daily sessions (distance/time where possible)
  - Sets/reps for strength
  - Specific interval lengths and tempo durations
  - Parkrun/test day notes for Week 8
  - Week 11 finisher plan and Week 12 taper/run test
- I can tailor to equipment on hand (dumbbells, barbells, resistance bands) and your client’s schedule (days/tref)

Important notes before starting
- Pre-workout: Ensure prn use of a reliever inhaler as prescribed, and have it accessible during every session.
- Warm-up: Emphasize a 10-minute dynamic warm-up (see weekly specifics). For cold days, consider indoor options or mask/face covering to warm air; if symptoms arise, pause and use inhaler, switch to a lighter session.
- EIA management: If symptoms (wheezing, chest tightness, cough) occur during a session, stop, use inhaler, and reassess after 5–10 minutes. If symptoms persist or worsen, seek medical advice.
- Progression principle: The plan increases volume gradually (about 10–15% per week) with some lighter weeks to accommodate adaptation and reduce injury risk.
- Injury/overload signs: If joint pain, persistent fatigue, or persistent breathlessness beyond expected EIA symptoms occur, scale back and consult.

- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Increased running blocks, extend continuous running gradually, reinforce pacing
